lesson.summary: Introduction to C: History, Characteristics and Classification
points: Dennis Ritchie developed C at Bell Labs in the early 1970s, building on B in the Unix environment.
C is general purpose, procedural and imperative; it is normally compiled.
Portability needs care with implementation-dependent behavior. Middle-level is an informal classroom label, not an ISO language category.

archive_evidence.history: Ritchie cites near and far pointers as extensions introduced for particular processors. Such extensions can tie a program to one environment.
archive_evidence.source: Dennis Ritchie, The Development of the C Language

archive_evidence.history: The team designed C to work with an operating system, so that a program could interact with files and use facilities beyond the language itself.
archive_evidence.source: Dennis Ritchie, The Development of the C Language

archive_evidence.history: Portability concerns moving source between environments. Different type limits or implementation choices can affect behavior. Check documented limits and avoid undocumented assumptions.
archive_evidence.source: GNU C Language Introduction and Reference Manual

archive_evidence.history: Use documented standard facilities when the same code must work in several environments. Isolate platform-specific features so they can be reviewed and adapted.
archive_evidence.source: GNU C Language Introduction and Reference Manual

archive_evidence.history: When code assumes a particular numeric range, identify the required range and check what the target implementation actually provides.
archive_evidence.source: GNU C Language Introduction and Reference Manual
